referenceMachine: 3M M56 (Series 500). Its public maintenance manual (M56 PAR 1-70) and the 1968 AES convention paper on the two-inch 16-track recorder are used as engineering benchmarks. No hardware was measured. This is not a claim of equivalence to that product.
status: documentation-derived; not validated against hardware; not listened to

evidence.referenceDbfs: assumed: host convention that operating level (0 VU, +4 dBm) sits at -18 dBFS
evidence.format.trackWidthInches: standard: 70 mil tracks of the two-inch 16-track format; not stated in the manual text read
evidence.tape.coatingThicknessMicrons: assumed: about 0.5 mil oxide for the low-noise tape the manual says the machine was aligned for (3M 202/203); thickness not verified
evidence.tape.hd3PercentAtCal: published: maintenance manual distortion test, 3 percent third harmonic at 1 kHz with the linearizer off
evidence.tape.hd3CalLevelDb: published: that test uses +10 dBm input, 6 dB above the +4 dBm operating level
evidence.tape.linearizer: published: under 0.8 percent third harmonic with the linearizer on at the same level; 0.7 chosen below the limit
evidence.tape.bias: published: 120 kHz bias, set 4 dB over peak at 15 kHz; recorded for reference, bias is not simulated as a signal
evidence.head.headBumpWavelengthInches: assumed: head contour dimensions are not in the manual; 0.30 inch puts the bump near 50 Hz at 15 ips
evidence.head.headBumpGainDb: assumed: 1.8 dB, inside the published +2 dB allowance at 30-50 Hz. The manual allows a larger low-frequency excursion than the 24-track's published flat-to-25 Hz response, so this machine is given the larger bump
evidence.electronics.transformers: published: AES paper describes input and output transformers and a transformer-coupled 600 ohm line amplifier; applying the same core model to the input transformer is an assumption
evidence.electronics.maxOutputDb: published: line amplifier maximum +28 dBm, 24 dB above operating level; distortion under 1 percent from 30 Hz to 15 kHz at that level, 0.8 percent at 30 Hz chosen
evidence.electronics.highpassHz: assumed: amplifier coupling corner is not given
evidence.transport.flutterComponents: assumed: component rates are placeholders; capstan and idler dimensions are not in the manual text read. Only the band totals are tied to published limits
evidence.speeds.equalization: published: NAB-format calibration tapes at 7.5 and 15 ips, with time constants from the NAB standard. The 30 ips curve is an assumption: the manual text read gives none, and 17.5 microseconds is the usual 30 ips standard
evidence.speeds.playbackHfCornerHz: assumed: at 15 ips the corner is set so the response is about 1 dB down at 15 kHz, half the published -2 dB tolerance, which is published only to 15 kHz (the 24-track's survey figure runs to 20 kHz). 7.5 and 30 ips are assumptions
evidence.speeds.flutter: derived: low band set to 60 percent of the published limits (0.04 percent at 15 ips, 0.07 at 7.5 ips, 0.5-300 Hz); scrape band from the AES paper's 0.075 percent wideband maximum less the low band, also at 60 percent. 30 ips has no published figure and reuses 15 ips
evidence.speeds.snrDb: assumed: the manual describes the noise test but prints no figure
evidence.speeds.publishedResponse: published: overall record tolerance, plus or minus 2 VU from 100 Hz to 15 kHz at 15 ips (to 10 kHz at 7.5 ips) and +2/-4 VU at 30 and 50 Hz, referred to 700 Hz
